# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura KS-822 PASS 1 (tier 1)** — PR #835 @ `04994288a` on merge-base `051bca051` (2026-09-06 06:53→07:14 AEST, ~40 min INSIDE a ~45 box; own `--shared` clone detached at the SHA, farmed `node_modules` with `require.resolve` inside it and `packages/shared/dist` COPIED not symlinked because `generate-openapi` builds shared; 16 tampers each shown applied by md5 + numstat + marker, the harness ABORTING once on a `perl -i` missing `-p` rather than passing a phantom green; two probes quarantined by rename; 24 listeners before/after; 27 evidence files) | 1 | **1.00** | 1.00 | **NO GO on ONE Major, and every one of the six items' claims HELD — all thirteen re-derived EXACT, the +28 exact in both directions, the yaml regenerated and byte-identical, the merge fact re-derived; it did NOT inherit the builder's wrong base and found a SECOND route to it (the builder's local develop is stale). The Major is the round's own: the contract this PR ships contradicts itself about the behaviour this PR changed — the F-4 prose ('filtered out, not refused') never revisited when F-5 made it a refusal two commits later — found by PARSING the hard-wrapped yaml after its own single-line grep nearly reported the enumeration absent (self-corrected in the open). EXPLAINED the builder's 5→6 miss with a condition-shaped tamper that reds 5 with the F-8 guard green: the guard is a SOURCE-TEXT guard that cannot see a rule stop working while its literal stays. Plant (a) against the F-8 reader was SILENT (49/49 green with the span wrong, both controls passing). The boundary hunt FOUND something: `scope=''`/`' '`/`',,,'` all mint the ENTIRE allow-list undriven, and `['*']` bypasses RULE 5. Drove the three new refusals live on the WIRE. And the finding that matters most, pre-existing and found only because it harvested the rendered page like a browser: the consent page cannot POST itself back (`oauth.ts:1197` emits the redirect URI as the hidden client_id) — reported, NOT sized, with the bearing on F-7 stated (all three entry points agree AT THE RESOLVER, never through the page). NOT-TESTED led with the platform suites and the schema change, then the page in a browser, the mocked DB, the refresh grant (KS-823), and that the MERGED result was never built.** |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent | **s136 — the KS-822 round (F-2d/F-4/F-5/F-6/F-7/F-8), PR #835** (`743863d4d` → `04994288a`, 2026-09-05 19:5x→20:46Z; six commits, 5 files +483/−27, 550 → 578 in place) | 1 | **0.75** | 0.75 | **All six items built with red-proofs whose SET and COUNT were predicted first and matched — and the one that did not match (F-5, 5 predicted / 6 measured) REPORTED AS A MISS rather than adjusted; F-2d's loosened-case-goes-green half run unprompted; F-7 with TWO isolating tampers because one would conflate the halves; F-8's header claim corrected and its enforceable half enforced with two controls and its limit MEASURED (a reused message is invisible) — and that limit then let F-6 through and was named as doing so; the item-0 consumer enumeration with a 39-hit control that produced KS-835; the five ruled lines lifted to KS-836/837 rather than left to die; a hand-typed 'four' REMOVED rather than corrected; its own orphan `' +` and its own control byte in a commit message both disclosed; every tamper reversed by the inverse edit with the hash checked.** Deductions: **F-QA-1 (Major, INTRODUCED)** — the contract shipping in the PR contradicts itself on the exact behaviour the PR changed, the F-4 sentence never revisited when F-5 landed, in the artefact F-8 exist

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
